subject_title: Ganita Prakash (NCERT Grade 8 Mathematics - Part II)

questions.question_text: What is the fraction 3/5 expressed as a percentage?
Express 0.08 as a percentage.
Convert 7/20 into a percentage and explain the step-by-step conversion method.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: To convert a fraction to percentage, multiply by 100: (7/20) * 100 = 7 * 5 = 35%.

questions.question_text: Surya prepared 60 ml of orange paint where red paint made up 3/4 of the total volume. Calculate the volume of red paint in ml and express it as a percentage.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Percentage of red paint = (3/4) * 100 = 75%. Volume of red paint = 75% of 60 ml = (75/100) * 60 = 45 ml.

questions.question_text: In a school of 500 students, 45% are boys and the remaining are girls. If 20% of the boys and 30% of the girls participate in a science fair, find: (i) total number of boys, (ii) total number of girls, (iii) total number of students participating in the science fair.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Boys = 45% of 500 = 225. (ii) Girls = 500 - 225 = 275. (iii) Participating boys = 20% of 225 = 45; Participating girls = 30% of 275 = 82.5 (or 83 rounded). Total participants = 45 + 82.5 = 127.5 (or 128).

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: Eesha scored 42 out of 50 in English and 70 out of 80 in Science. (a) Calculate her percentage score in English. (b) Calculate her percentage score in Science. (c) In which subject did she perform better relatively?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) English % = (42/50)*100 = 84%. (b) Science % = (70/80)*100 = 87.5%. (c) Eesha performed better in Science because 87.5% > 84%.

questions.question_text: Using benchmark percentages, what is 15% of 80?
According to the percentage symmetry property, 16% of 25 is equal to:
Prove algebraically that x% of y is always equal to y% of x.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: x% of y = (x/100)*y = (x*y)/100. y% of x = (y/100)*x = (y*x)/100. Since multiplication is commutative (x*y = y*x), both expressions yield identical results.

questions.question_text: Compute 35% of 240 mentally using benchmark percentages (50%, 10%, 5%). Show all mental calculation steps clearly.

A student uses a visual bar model divided into 10 equal blocks to represent $400. (i) What dollar amount does each block represent? (ii) Shade blocks to represent 35% of $400 and calculate the value. (iii) Explain how the bar model helps visualize percentages greater than 100%.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Each block represents 10% of $400 = $40. (ii) 35% requires 3.5 blocks = 3.5 * $40 = $140. (iii) For percentages > 100%, additional full bars are added alongside the base bar (e.g., 250% requires 2 full bars and a half bar).

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: Rohan wants to calculate 84% of 50. Instead of multiplying 84 by 0.84, he calculates 50% of 84. (a) Is Rohan's approach mathematically valid? State the law used. (b) Calculate 50% of 84. (c) What is 84% of 50?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Yes, it is valid based on the Percentage Symmetry Law (x% of y = y% of x). (b) 50% of 84 = 84 / 2 = 42. (c) 84% of 50 = 42.

questions.question_text: If a quantity grows by 150%, its final value relative to the original base value is:
Express 2.75 as a percentage.
A town's population was 12,000 in 2020 and grew to 18,000 in 2024. Express the new population as a percentage of the original population.
A factory produced 400 units in January. Production increased by 125% in February. Calculate: (i) the increase in production units, (ii) the total production in February.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Increase = 125% of 400 = (125/100) * 400 = 500 units. (ii) February production = 400 + 500 = 900 units (which is 225% of January production).

questions.question_text: An excursion group has 200 total students. 40% are Grade 8 students, and the rest are Grade 9 students. If 60% of the Grade 8 students are girls, calculate: (i) number of Grade 8 students, (ii) number of Grade 9 students, (iii) number of Grade 8 girls, (iv) number of Grade 8 boys.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Grade 8 = 40% of 200 = 80. (ii) Grade 9 = 200 - 80 = 120. (iii) Grade 8 girls = 60% of 80 = 48. (iv) Grade 8 boys = 80 - 48 = 32.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A farmer's wheat yield was 50 bags last year. This year, due to good rainfall, the yield increased to 130 bags. (a) What is the percentage increase in yield? (b) Express this year's yield as a percentage of last year's yield.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Increase = 130 - 50 = 80 bags. Percentage increase = (80/50)*100 = 160%. (b) This year's yield as % of last year = (130/50)*100 = 260%.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - KYC Product Analysis & Ingredient Concentration

questions.question_text: Mix A contains 12 g badam powder in 150 g mix. What is the percentage of badam powder?
Mix B contains 40 g badam powder in 400 g mix. Which mix has a higher almond concentration?
Why must ingredient proportions on food packaging be converted to percentages per 100g rather than comparing raw weight grams directly?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Raw weights depend on total package size. Converting to percentage standardizes the base to 100g, allowing fair relative concentration comparisons across different package sizes.

questions.question_text: A 250 g fruit juice pack contains 35 g natural fruit pulp. A 400 g fruit juice pack contains 52 g natural fruit pulp. Determine which pack offers a richer fruit content by calculating percentages.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Pack 1 % = (35 / 250) * 100 = 14%. Pack 2 % = (52 / 400) * 100 = 13%. Pack 1 offers a richer fruit content (14% > 13%).

questions.question_text: A health drink powder packaging lists ingredients for a 500 g jar: Cocoa powder 75 g, Milk solids 200 g, Sugar 175 g, Added vitamins 50 g. (i) Calculate the percentage share of each ingredient. (ii) Verify that the sum of all percentages equals 100%.

Case Scenario: A consumer nutrition report compares two cereal brands. Brand X has 18 g protein per 200 g serving. Brand Y has 27 g protein per 300 g serving. (a) Calculate protein percentage in Brand X. (b) Calculate protein percentage in Brand Y. (c) Compare the two brands.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Brand X % = (18/200)*100 = 9%. (b) Brand Y % = (27/300)*100 = 9%. (c) Both brands have identical protein concentration (9%).

questions.question_text: An item costing $100 is marked up by 35% and then discounted by 30%. The final selling price is:
In the scenario above, the shopkeeper incurs a net loss of:
Explain the root cause of why a 35% mark-up followed by a 30% discount does NOT result in a 5% net profit.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Root cause: The 35% mark-up is calculated on the lower Cost Price, whereas the 30% discount is applied to the higher Marked Price. Discounts applied to larger base values outweigh percentage mark-ups on smaller base values.

questions.question_text: A dealer buys a watch for $800. He marks it up by 25% and then offers a discount of 20% on the marked price. Find: (i) Marked Price, (ii) Selling Price, (iii) Profit or Loss percentage.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Marked Price = 800 + 25% of 800 = 800 + 200 = $1000. (ii) Selling Price = 1000 - 20% of 1000 = 1000 - 200 = $800. (iii) SP = CP ($800), so there is 0% profit and 0% loss.

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper bought 50 shirts at $200 each. He sold 30 shirts at a profit of 20%, 15 shirts at a profit of 10%, and the remaining 5 shirts at a loss of 10%. Calculate: (i) Total Cost Price, (ii) Total Selling Price, (iii) Overall net profit percentage.

Case Scenario: A bicycle store offers two promotional schemes on a $500 bicycle: Scheme A: Single discount of 30%. Scheme B: Successive discounts of 20% and then 10%. (a) Find final price under Scheme A. (b) Find final price under Scheme B. (c) Which scheme is better for the customer?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Scheme A Price = 500 * (1 - 0.30) = $350. (b) Scheme B Price = 500 * 0.80 * 0.90 = 400 * 0.90 = $360. (c) Scheme A is better for the customer as it is $10 cheaper ($350 < $360).

questions.question_text: In a right-angled triangle with legs a=6 and b=8, the hypotenuse c is:
Which of the following integer sets forms a Baudhāyana triple?
State the Baudhāyana-Pythagoras Theorem as recorded in the ancient Śulba-Sūtras.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In any right-angled triangle, the area of the square constructed on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas of the squares constructed on the other two legs: a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

questions.question_text: Check whether the triangle with side lengths 8 cm, 15 cm, and 17 cm is right-angled. Show full algebraic verification.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Calculate squares: 8^2 = 64, 15^2 = 225, 17^2 = 289. Sum of legs: 64 + 225 = 289. Since 8^2 + 15^2 = 17^2, the triangle is right-angled.

questions.question_text: Find the side length and area of a rhombus whose diagonals bisect each other at right angles with lengths 24 units and 70 units.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Half-diagonals are a = 24/2 = 12 and b = 70/2 = 35. Side s = sqrt(12^2 + 35^2) = sqrt(144 + 1225) = sqrt(1369) = 37 units. Area of rhombus = 0.5 * d1 * d2 = 0.5 * 24 * 70 = 840 sq units.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A 17 m long ladder leans against a vertical wall such that its foot is 8 m away from the base of the wall. (a) Identify the hypotenuse. (b) Calculate how high up the wall the ladder reaches.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) The ladder forms the hypotenuse c = 17 m. (b) Height a = sqrt(17^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(289 - 64) = sqrt(225) = 15 m.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Square Diagonals & Properties of sqrt(2)

questions.question_text: The diagonal of a square with side length 'a' is given by:
The numerical value of sqrt(2) lies strictly between:
If the hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle is sqrt(72) cm, find the length of its legs.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In isosceles right triangle, c^2 = 2a^2 => (sqrt(72))^2 = 2a^2 => 72 = 2a^2 => a^2 = 36 => a = 6 cm.

questions.question_text: Explain why constructing a square on the diagonal of a unit square doubles its surface area, referencing Baudhāyana's Śulba-Sūtra.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A unit square has area 1*1 = 1. Its diagonal d = sqrt(1^2 + 1^2) = sqrt(2). A square built on side d has area d^2 = (sqrt(2))^2 = 2, which is exactly double the original area.

questions.question_text: A square park has side length 50 m. A straight diagonal walking track connects opposite corners. (i) Calculate the track length in surd form. (ii) Using sqrt(2) approx 1.414, calculate track length to 2 decimal places. (iii) Calculate how much distance is saved by walking along the diagonal instead of around two sides.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Diagonal = 50*sqrt(2) m. (ii) 50 * 1.414 = 70.70 m. (iii) Two sides distance = 50 + 50 = 100 m. Distance saved = 100 - 70.70 = 29.30 m.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: An artist designs a square glass tile of side 10 cm. She inserts two diagonal lead wires across the tile. (a) Find the length of one lead wire in surd form. (b) Find total length of both lead wires used.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Length of one diagonal = 10*sqrt(2) cm. (b) Total wire length = 2 * 10*sqrt(2) = 20*sqrt(2) approx 28.28 cm.

questions.question_text: In the 4-triangle dissection proof of side (a+b), the unshaded inner tilted shape has side length:
The total area of the outer bounding square in the dissection proof is:
Summarize the key observation in rearranging four right triangles inside a square of side (a+b).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In Arrangement 1, unshaded area is c^2. In Arrangement 2, the same four triangles leave unshaded areas a^2 and b^2. Equating unshaded regions proves c^2 = a^2 + b^2.

questions.question_text: Construct a step-by-step geometric explanation showing how combining two squares of side 3 units and 4 units creates a square of side 5 units.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Square 1 area = 3^2 = 9. Square 2 area = 4^2 = 16. Combined area = 9 + 16 = 25. Constructing a square on the hypotenuse of right triangle with legs 3 and 4 gives side sqrt(25) = 5 units.

questions.question_text: Show how to construct a square of area 5 square units starting from a unit square of side 1 unit using Baudhāyana's right-triangle extension steps.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Step 1: Unit square side 1 has diagonal sqrt(2). Step 2: Build right triangle with legs 1 and sqrt(2) -> hypotenuse is sqrt(1+2) = sqrt(3). Step 3: Build right triangle with legs 1 and 2 -> hypotenuse is sqrt(1^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(5). Building a square on this hypotenuse gives area (sqrt(5))^2 = 5 sq units.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A carpenter cuts four identical right triangular wooden pieces with leg lengths 5 cm and 12 cm. (a) Calculate hypotenuse c. (b) Find the area of the central square formed when arranged inside a 17 cm outer square.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) c = sqrt(5^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(25 + 144) = 13 cm. (b) Outer square side = 5 + 12 = 17 cm. Central square side = c = 13 cm, so its area = 13^2 = 169 sq cm.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Scaled Triples & Geometric Geometry Problems

questions.question_text: If primitive triple is (3, 4, 5), scaling by k=3 gives the scaled triple:
Scaling a triple (a, b, c) by integer factor k multiplies the hypotenuse area by:
Verify algebraically that scaling the Baudhāyana triple (5, 12, 13) by k=4 satisfies a^2 + b^2 = c^2.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Scaled triple = (20, 48, 52). Verification: 20^2 + 48^2 = 400 + 2304 = 2704. 52^2 = 2704. Equation holds.

questions.question_text: A rectangular field measures 30 m by 40 m. Find the length of its diagonal and verify that its sides form a scaled version of (3, 4, 5).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Diagonal = sqrt(30^2 + 40^2) = sqrt(900 + 1600) = sqrt(2500) = 50 m. Dividing (30, 40, 50) by 10 gives primitive triple (3, 4, 5), so scale factor k=10.

questions.question_text: A flagship pole 24 m high snapped at a height 'x' above ground during a storm, such that its top touches ground 12 m away from its base. (i) Set up the right triangle relation. (ii) Calculate the height 'x' where it snapped.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Total pole = 24. Remaining standing height = x. Fallen hypotenuse = 24 - x. Ground base = 12. Relation: x^2 + 12^2 = (24 - x)^2. (ii) x^2 + 144 = 576 - 48x + x^2 => 48x = 432 => x = 9 m. Pole broke at 9 m height.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: An architect designs a triangular roof truss with sides 15 m, 20 m, and 25 m. (a) Is the roof truss a right triangle? (b) Identify the primitive triple and scale factor used.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) 15^2 + 20^2 = 225 + 400 = 625 = 25^2, so yes it is a right triangle. (b) Primitive triple is (3, 4, 5) with scale factor k=5.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Ancient Historical Problems & Līlāvatī Applications

questions.question_text: In Bhāskarāchārya's Līlāvatī Lotus problem, if lotus peep height is 1 unit and displacement is 3 units, lake depth is:
The verse 1.13 in Baudhāyana Śulba-Sūtras explicitly lists which of the following triples?
State the algebraic equation set up for Bhāskarāchārya's lotus problem where lake depth is x, stem peep is h, and sway distance is d.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Vertical leg = x, horizontal leg = d, hypotenuse = x + h. Equation: d^2 + x^2 = (x + h)^2.

questions.question_text: Solve the lotus problem when the lotus peep height above water is 2 cm and horizontal displacement when submerged is 8 cm.

A peacock is perched on top of a 9 m high pillar. A snake is spotted at a distance of 27 m from the foot of the pillar moving towards its base. The peacock pounces on the snake when both cover equal distance. (i) Set up right triangle equation. (ii) Calculate distance from pillar base where pounce occurs.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Let pounce point be at distance 'x' from pillar base. Snake distance covered = 27 - x. Peacock flight distance (hypotenuse) = 27 - x. Vertical pillar = 9. Right triangle: 9^2 + x^2 = (27 - x)^2. (ii) 81 + x^2 = 729 - 54x + x^2 => 54x = 648 => x = 12 m. Pounce occurs 12 m from pillar base.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: An Indian heritage research scholar analyzes ancient Śulba-Sūtras altar geometry. An altar construction uses triples (12, 35, 37). (a) Verify that (12, 35, 37) is a valid Baudhāyana triple. (b) Calculate hypotenuse square area.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) 12^2 + 35^2 = 144 + 1225 = 1369. 37^2 = 1369. Equation holds. (b) Hypotenuse square area = 37^2 = 1369 sq units.

questions.question_text: If $120 is divided in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5, the total number of parts is:
In the ratio share above, the largest share is:
State the rule for partitioning a total quantity Q into a multi-term ratio a : b : c.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Total parts = a + b + c. Individual shares are calculated as (a/total)*Q, (b/total)*Q, and (c/total)*Q.

questions.question_text: The three interior angles of a triangle are in the multi-term ratio 3 : 4 : 5. Find the measure of each angle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°. Total parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12. Angle 1 = (3/12)*180 = 45°. Angle 2 = (4/12)*180 = 60°. Angle 3 = (5/12)*180 = 75°.

questions.question_text: A concrete mixture requires cement, sand, and gravel in the ratio 1 : 2 : 4 by weight. (i) How much of each ingredient is needed to prepare 350 kg of concrete? (ii) If 10 kg extra cement is added, find the new ratio.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Total parts = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 parts. Cement = (1/7)*350 = 50 kg. Sand = (2/7)*350 = 100 kg. Gravel = (4/7)*350 = 200 kg. (ii) New cement = 50 + 10 = 60 kg. New ratio = 60 : 100 : 200 = 3 : 5 : 10.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: Three partners A, B, and C invest in a business in the ratio 4 : 5 : 6. The total annual profit earned is $45,000. (a) Calculate partner A's profit share. (b) Calculate partner C's profit share.
Representative Fraction (RF) is defined as:
On a map with RF 1 : 50,000, a map distance of 1 cm represents a real ground distance of:
Why is Representative Fraction (RF) considered a unitless ratio?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: RF is unitless because both numerator (map distance) and denominator (ground distance) are expressed in the same physical units (e.g., centimeters), so units cancel out.

questions.question_text: On a geographical map with scale RF 1 : 6,000,000, two towns are separated by 3.5 cm. Calculate the actual ground distance between the towns in kilometers.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Ground distance = 3.5 cm * 6,000,000 = 21,000,000 cm. Converting to meters: 21,000,000 / 100 = 210,000 m. Converting to km: 210,000 / 1000 = 210 km.

questions.question_text: A real railway track between two cities is 180 km long. (i) Convert 180 km into centimeters. (ii) If the track measures 4.5 cm on a state map, calculate the RF scale of the map. (iii) Find map distance on the same map for a 60 km sub-section.

Case Scenario: A city surveyor uses a blueprint map with scale 1 : 200 to design a park. On the map, the park rectangle measures 15 cm by 10 cm. (a) Find actual ground dimensions in meters. (b) Calculate actual park area in square meters.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Ground length = 15 * 200 = 3000 cm = 30 m. Ground width = 10 * 200 = 2000 cm = 20 m. (b) Ground area = 30 * 20 = 600 sq meters.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Pie Charts & Central Sector Angle Computations

questions.question_text: The sum of central angles of all sectors in a pie chart is always equal to:
If a category represents 25% of the total, its central angle in a pie chart is:
State the standard formula used to compute the central sector angle for a category in a pie chart.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Central Angle = (Category Frequency / Total Sum of Frequencies) * 360°.

questions.question_text: In a survey of 40 students, 12 chose Grade A, 10 Grade B, 8 Grade C, 6 Grade D, and 4 Grade E. Calculate the central angles for Grade A and Grade B.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Total N = 40. Grade A angle = (12/40)*360° = 108°. Grade B angle = (10/40)*360° = 90°.

questions.question_text: A family's monthly budget of $3600 is spent as follows: Food $1200, Rent $900, Education $600, Savings $500, Miscellaneous $400. (i) Calculate central angles for all 5 sectors. (ii) Verify that the sum of angles equals 360°.

Case Scenario: A pie chart shows student transport modes: Bus (144° sector angle), Walking (108° sector angle), Bicycle (108° sector angle). Total school population is 500 students. (a) Calculate percentage using Bus. (b) Find exact student count walking to school.
Which of the following pairs of variables are in inverse proportion?
options: Speed and travel time for a fixed distance
Side length of square and perimeter
Weight of apples and total cost
questions.correct_answer: Speed and travel time for a fixed distance

questions.question_text: If x and y vary inversely, their governing mathematical law is:
Differentiate clearly between direct proportion and inverse proportion using product vs quotient relations.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In direct proportion, the ratio quotient x/y is constant (as x increases, y increases). In inverse proportion, the product x*y is constant (as x increases, y decreases proportionally).

questions.question_text: If 20 workers take 4 days to complete laying a road, how many days will 10 workers take? Show full inverse proportion product equation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Workers (x) and days (y) vary inversely: x1 * y1 = x2 * y2 => 20 * 4 = 10 * y2 => 80 = 10 * y2 => y2 = 8 days.

questions.question_text: A car traveling at a constant speed of 60 km/h takes 4 hours to complete a journey. (i) Calculate the total fixed journey distance. (ii) How long will the same journey take if speed is increased to 80 km/h? (iii) What speed is required to complete the journey in 3 hours?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Distance = speed * time = 60 * 4 = 240 km. (ii) Time at 80 km/h = 240 / 80 = 3 hours. (iii) Required speed for 3 hours = 240 / 3 = 80 km/h.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A school hostel has food provisions for 120 students lasting 30 days. If 30 new students join the hostel, (a) Set up inverse proportion equation. (b) Calculate how many days the food provisions will last now.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Advanced Workforce & Pipe Filling Applications

questions.question_text: If 6 identical pipes fill a water tank in 80 minutes, 4 pipes will fill it in:
To complete a project in 18 days instead of 24 days with initial 15 workers, required workers are:
If 15 workers build a wall in 24 days, how many EXTRA workers must be hired to complete the work in 18 days?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 15 * 24 = W * 18 => 360 = 18W => W = 20 workers. Additional workers needed = 20 - 15 = 5 extra workers.

questions.question_text: A water reservoir is filled by 8 pipes in 1 hour 15 minutes (75 minutes). Calculate how long it will take to fill the reservoir if 3 pipes get clogged and only 5 pipes function.

A contractor estimated that 30 workers could construct a bridge span in 40 days. After 10 days of work, 10 additional workers joined. (i) Calculate remaining man-days needed after day 10. (ii) Calculate how many days the remaining work will take. (iii) Find total days taken for full construction.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Work done in 10 days = 30 * 10 = 300 man-days. Remaining work = (30 * 40) - 300 = 1200 - 300 = 900 man-days. (ii) New workforce = 30 + 10 = 40 workers. Remaining days = 900 / 40 = 22.5 days. (iii) Total time = 10 + 22.5 = 32.5 days.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A printing press uses 5 identical automated printing machines to print 10,000 books in 12 days. (a) If 1 machine breaks down, how long will 4 machines take? (b) How many machines are needed to complete the printing in 6 days?
Self-similarity in geometry refers to a property where:
options: Small parts resemble the whole structure
questions.correct_answer: Small parts resemble the whole structure

questions.question_text: Which of the following natural objects exhibits botanical fractal branching?
Define a fractal and list two examples found in nature and two in human art/architecture.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A fractal is a complex geometric structure that exhibits self-similarity across scales. Nature: Fern fronds, coastlines, trees. Art/Architecture: Indian temple shikharas, rangoli designs.

questions.question_text: Explain how a tree branch illustrates self-similarity across multiple scale levels.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The main tree trunk splits into major branches, each major branch splits into smaller boughs, boughs split into twigs, and twigs split into leaf veins. Each sub-level mirrors the overall branching structure of the whole tree.

questions.question_text: Describe step-by-step construction of the Sierpinski Carpet from Step 0 to Step 1. (i) State initial shape at Step 0. (ii) Describe grid partition in Step 1. (iii) Calculate remaining squares count and central hole count at Step 1.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Step 0 starts with a solid unit square. (ii) Divide the square into a 3x3 grid of 9 equal sub-squares. (iii) Remove the 1 central sub-square (hole = 1). Remaining solid small squares = 8.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: An architectural designer studies traditional Indian temple spires (Shikharas) and notes miniature spire replicas decorating the main spire. (a) What geometric property does this architecture embody? (b) State one mathematical advantage of fractal structural designs.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Self-similarity / fractal geometry. (b) Fractal design maximizes surface area and structural balance while maintaining compact overall volume.

questions.question_text: The number of remaining solid small squares at step n in the Sierpinski Carpet is given by:
The remaining area at step n in the Sierpinski Carpet relative to initial unit area is:
Calculate the number of remaining small squares at Step 3 of the Sierpinski Carpet.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Formula R_n = 8^n. For Step 3, R_3 = 8^3 = 512 small squares.

questions.question_text: Calculate the remaining area fraction at Step 2 of the Sierpinski Carpet starting from a square of area 81 cm^2.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Remaining area fraction = (8/9)^2 = 64/81. Remaining area = 81 * (64/81) = 64 cm^2.

questions.question_text: Derive the formula for total cumulative holes H_n in the Sierpinski Carpet at step n. (i) State new holes added at step n. (ii) Write the recursive equation H_(n+1) = H_n + R_n. (iii) Calculate total holes for Step 1, Step 2, and Step 3.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Each remaining square R_n = 8^n adds 1 new hole in step n+1. (ii) H_(n+1) = H_n + 8^n. (iii) Step 1: H1 = 1. Step 2: H2 = 1 + 8 = 9. Step 3: H3 = 9 + 64 = 73 holes. Formula H_n = (8^n - 1) / 7.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A digital artist constructs a Sierpinski Carpet up to Step 2. (a) How many small square holes of all sizes are cut out in total? (b) What fraction of original area is removed after Step 2?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Total holes H2 = 1 + 8 = 9 holes. (b) Remaining area = (8/9)^2 = 64/81. Removed area fraction = 1 - 64/81 = 17/81.

questions.question_text: At Step 1 of the Sierpinski Triangle, joining side midpoints removes how many central inverted triangles?
The number of remaining upright small triangles at step n in Sierpinski Triangle is:
Calculate the number of remaining small upright triangles at Step 3 of the Sierpinski Triangle sequence.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Formula T_n = 3^n. For Step 3, T_3 = 3^3 = 27 triangles.

questions.question_text: Starting with an equilateral triangle of area 64 cm^2, calculate the remaining solid area at Step 1 and Step 2 of the Sierpinski Triangle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: At each step, 1/4 of area is removed, keeping 3/4. Step 1 area = 64 * (3/4) = 48 cm^2. Step 2 area = 48 * (3/4) = 36 cm^2.

questions.question_text: Compare the Sierpinski Carpet and Sierpinski Triangle: (i) Base polygon for each. (ii) Sub-division rule for each. (iii) Remaining shape count formula for each. (iv) Remaining area fraction formula for each.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Carpet: Square; Triangle: Equilateral triangle. (ii) Carpet: 3x3 grid (9 parts, remove 1); Triangle: Midpoint connection (4 parts, remove 1). (iii) Carpet count = 8^n; Triangle count = 3^n. (iv) Carpet area = (8/9)^n; Triangle area = (3/4)^n.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A geometry student draws Sierpinski Triangle up to Step 2 on a poster. (a) How many small central inverted triangle holes are removed in Step 2 alone? (b) What is total count of remaining solid triangles at Step 2?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Step 1 removes 1 hole. Step 2 removes 1 hole from each of 3 remaining triangles = 3 new holes. (b) Total remaining solid triangles at Step 2 = 3^2 = 9.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Koch Snowflake & Infinite Perimeter vs Bounded Area

questions.question_text: At each iteration step of the Koch Snowflake, each line segment is replaced by how many smaller segments?
Starting with an equilateral triangle of perimeter 3 units, the perimeter at step n of the Koch Snowflake is:
Calculate the perimeter of the Koch Snowflake at Step 2 starting from an initial equilateral triangle of side length 1 unit.
Explain the mathematical paradox of the Koch Snowflake regarding its perimeter and its enclosed area.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: As iteration step n approaches infinity, perimeter P_n = 3*(4/3)^n grows infinitely large without bound. However, the snowflake fits entirely inside a finite bounding circle, so its enclosed area remains strictly finite and bounded.

questions.question_text: Trace the Koch Snowflake generation from Step 0 to Step 2: (i) State side count at Step 0, Step 1, Step 2. (ii) Write the side count formula N_n = 3 * 4^n. (iii) If initial side length is 9 cm, find side segment length at Step 2. (iv) Calculate perimeter at Step 2.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Step 0: 3 sides. Step 1: 12 sides. Step 2: 48 sides. (ii) N_n = 3 * 4^n. (iii) Initial side L0 = 9 cm. L1 = 9/3 = 3 cm. L2 = 3/3 = 1 cm. (iv) Perimeter P2 = N2 * L2 = 48 * 1 cm = 48 cm.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A snowflake fractal antenna is designed for wireless signal reception. (a) What formula gives total side segment count at Step 3? (b) Calculate total side count at Step 3.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) N_n = 3 * 4^n. (b) For Step 3, N3 = 3 * 4^3 = 3 * 64 = 192 side segments.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - 3D Solids, Folding Nets & Shortest Surface Paths

questions.question_text: A standard cube has how many distinct valid 2D planar nets?
To find the shortest path along the outer surface between two points on a 3D box, one should:
options: Unfold box into a 2D net and draw a straight line
questions.correct_answer: Unfold box into a 2D net and draw a straight line

questions.question_text: What is a planar net of a 3D solid figure? Give two examples.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A planar net is a 2D flat arrangement of connected polygon faces that folds along shared edges to form a 3D solid. Examples: 6-square T-net for a cube, 4-triangle net for a tetrahedron.

questions.question_text: An ant wants to crawl on the surface of a cuboid box of dimensions 6 cm x 4 cm x 3 cm from bottom corner A to top corner B on an adjacent face. Explain how unfolding the net yields the shortest surface path.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Unfolding adjacent faces flattened onto a 2D plane converts the surface path into a straight line hypotenuse connecting A and B across combined dimensions (e.g., legs 6+3 = 9 cm and 4 cm). Path length = sqrt(9^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(81 + 16) = sqrt(97) cm.

questions.question_text: Analyze a closed rectangular box measuring 10 cm long, 8 cm wide, and 6 cm high. (i) How many faces does its net contain and what are their dimensions? (ii) Calculate total surface area of the box using face areas. (iii) Draw a sketch description of a valid unfolded net layout.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) 6 rectangular faces: 2 of (10x8), 2 of (10x6), 2 of (8x6). (ii) Total surface area = 2*(10*8 + 10*6 + 8*6) = 2*(80 + 60 + 48) = 2*188 = 376 sq cm. (iii) Sketch description: A central column of 4 rectangles (10x8, 10x6, 10x8, 10x6) with 2 side wing rectangles (8x6) attached.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A cardboard box manufacturer designs a foldable gift box net with dimensions 12 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm. (a) Calculate total surface area of cardboard needed. (b) If 10% extra cardboard is wasted in folding flaps, find total cardboard sheet area required.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Surface area = 2*(12*5 + 12*4 + 5*4) = 2*(60 + 48 + 20) = 2*128 = 256 sq cm. (b) Wasted flaps = 10% of 256 = 25.6 sq cm. Total sheet area = 256 + 25.6 = 281.6 sq cm.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Arithmetic Mean & Visual Fulcrum Model

questions.question_text: The arithmetic mean of data points 4, 6, and 11 is:
On a dot plot number line, the arithmetic mean acts as a physical:
State the balance condition for the arithmetic mean on a horizontal number line.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sum of leftward distance deviations from the mean for points below mean equals sum of rightward distance deviations for points above mean.

questions.question_text: Data dots are placed on a number line at 10, 13, and 22. Find the mean and verify that total left deviations equal total right deviations.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Mean = (10 + 13 + 22) / 3 = 45 / 3 = 15. Left deviations below 15: (15-10) + (15-13) = 5 + 2 = 7. Right deviation above 15: (22-15) = 7. Left deviations (7) = Right deviations (7).

questions.question_text: Explain the meter stick fulcrum balance experiment: (i) Equal weight washers placed at 20 cm, 30 cm, and 70 cm. (ii) Calculate mean position. (iii) Show distance moment balance about pivot at 40 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Washers at 20, 30, 70. (ii) Mean = (20 + 30 + 70)/3 = 120/3 = 40 cm. (iii) Left moments = (40-20) + (40-30) = 20 + 10 = 30 cm. Right moment = (70-40) = 30 cm. Since 30 = 30, the meter stick balances horizontally at 40 cm.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: Five students score test marks: 12, 15, 18, 20, 25. (a) Calculate mean test score. (b) Find deviation of each score from mean and verify sum of deviations is 0.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Zero Total Deviation Law & Properties

questions.question_text: The sum of algebraic deviations of all data values from their arithmetic mean is:
For dataset {2, 8}, the mean is 5. Algebraic deviations (2-5) and (8-5) sum to:
State the Zero Total Deviation Law algebraically using summation notation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sum of (x_i - Mean) = 0 for i = 1 to N.

questions.question_text: Data values are 5, 8, 12, 15, x. The mean is 10. Find x using the Zero Total Deviation Law.
Prove mathematically that Sum(x_i - Mean) = 0 for any arbitrary N data points x1, x2, ..., xN.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sum(x_i - Mean) = (x1 - Mean) + (x2 - Mean) + ... + (xN - Mean) = (x1 + x2 + ... + xN) - N*Mean. Since Mean = (x1 + ... + xN)/N, N*Mean = (x1 + ... + xN). Therefore, Sum = (N*Mean) - (N*Mean) = 0.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: Four numbers are 14, 18, 22, 26. (a) Calculate the mean. (b) Calculate squared deviations for each number and sum them.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Uniform Data Transformations & Shifting Means

questions.question_text: If every data point in a set with mean 15 is increased by 5, the new mean becomes:
If every data point in a set with mean 12 is multiplied by 3, the new mean becomes:
State the effect on the arithmetic mean when (i) a constant 'k' is added to all values, (ii) all values are multiplied by 'k'.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) New Mean = Old Mean + k. (ii) New Mean = Old Mean * k.

questions.question_text: The mean mark of 10 students was 65. The teacher added 5 grace marks to every student and then doubled everyone's final score. Find the new mean mark.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: After adding 5 grace marks: Mean = 65 + 5 = 70. After doubling: New Mean = 70 * 2 = 140.

questions.question_text: The mean of 5 numbers is 18. If one number is removed, the mean of the remaining 4 numbers becomes 16. (i) Find original sum. (ii) Find new sum. (iii) Calculate the removed number.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Original sum = 5 * 18 = 90. (ii) New sum = 4 * 16 = 64. (iii) Removed number = 90 - 64 = 26.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A student scored 65, 72, 80, and 78 in four term exams. She wants her five-exam mean to be 75. (a) Calculate required total sum for 5 exams. (b) Find score needed in 5th exam.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Required sum = 5 * 75 = 375. Current sum = 65 + 72 + 80 + 78 = 295. (b) Required 5th exam score = 375 - 295 = 80.

questions.question_text: Class A (20 students) has mean height 145 cm. Class B (30 students) has mean height 150 cm. Combined mean height is:
Formula for combined mean of two groups N1 (mean X1) and N2 (mean X2) is:
Why is simple average of group means (X1 + X2)/2 invalid when group sample sizes N1 and N2 are unequal?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Simple average assumes equal weights. When N1 != N2, the group with larger sample size contributes more total observations, so weighted mean (N1*X1 + N2*X2)/(N1+N2) must be used.

questions.question_text: Group 1 has 10 workers earning average daily wage $200. Group 2 has 15 workers earning average daily wage $250. Calculate combined average daily wage.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Group 1 total wage = 10 * 200 = $2000. Group 2 total wage = 15 * 250 = $3750. Combined total wage = 2000 + 3750 = $5750. Total workers = 25. Combined average = 5750 / 25 = $230.

questions.question_text: A school has 3 sections in Grade 8: Section A (25 students, mean mark 70), Section B (35 students, mean mark 80), Section C (40 students, mean mark 75). (i) Find total marks scored by each section. (ii) Calculate total Grade 8 marks sum. (iii) Calculate overall Grade 8 combined mean mark.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Sec A sum = 25 * 70 = 1750. Sec B sum = 35 * 80 = 2800. Sec C sum = 40 * 75 = 3000. (ii) Total marks = 1750 + 2800 + 3000 = 7550. (iii) Total students = 25 + 35 + 40 = 100. Combined mean = 7550 / 100 = 75.5.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A company employs 8 junior engineers at mean salary $40,000 and 2 senior directors at mean salary $90,000. (a) Calculate combined mean salary of all 10 employees. (b) Explain why mean salary is pulled upward by director salaries.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Total salary = (8 * 40000) + (2 * 90000) = 320000 + 180000 = $500,000. Combined mean = 500000 / 10 = $50,000. (b) Extreme high values (outliers) pull the arithmetic mean toward them.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Line Graphs & Temporal Trend Analysis

questions.question_text: Line graphs are best suited for representing:
options: Continuous temporal data trends over time
questions.correct_answer: Continuous temporal data trends over time

questions.question_text: In a line graph plotting time vs temperature, slope of line segment indicates:
Why is uniform axis spacing crucial when drawing line graphs?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Uniform axis spacing ensures that visual line slopes accurately represent true mathematical rates of change without misleading distortion.

questions.question_text: A patient's body temperature is recorded every 2 hours from 8 AM to 4 PM: 37°C, 37.5°C, 38.5°C, 38°C, 37°C. Describe line graph trends and identify peak temperature time.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Temperatures rise steadily from 37°C at 8 AM to reach a peak of 38.5°C at 12 PM, then decrease steadily back to 37°C at 4 PM. Peak temperature occurred at 12 PM.

questions.question_text: Monthly temperature data (°C) for 6 months: Jan 12, Feb 15, Mar 20, Apr 26, May 32, Jun 35. (i) Calculate mean monthly temperature. (ii) Identify month-to-month period with steepest temperature rise. (iii) Calculate rate of change (°C/month) for steepest rise.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Sum = 12 + 15 + 20 + 26 + 32 + 35 = 140. Mean = 140 / 6 = 23.33°C. (ii) Rises: Jan-Feb (3), Feb-Mar (5), Mar-Apr (6), Apr-May (6), May-Jun (3). Steepest rises occur Mar-Apr and Apr-May (6°C rise). (iii) Rate = 6°C / month.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A solar power station tracks energy generation (kWh) across 4 hours: Hour 1 (50 kWh), Hour 2 (120 kWh), Hour 3 (180 kWh), Hour 4 (90 kWh). (a) Calculate total energy generated. (b) Find mean energy output per hour.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Total energy = 50 + 120 + 180 + 90 = 440 kWh. (b) Mean energy output = 440 / 4 = 110 kWh per hour.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Deconstructing 'Think of a Number' Tricks

questions.question_text: In the trick: Think of x, double it, add 8, divide by 2, subtract x, the final result is:
Using variable x to model number tricks proves that final outcome is independent of starting number when:
Deconstruct algebraically: Think of x, add 5, multiply by 2, subtract 10, divide by 2. State final expression.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: x -> x+5 -> 2(x+5)=2x+10 -> (2x+10)-10=2x -> 2x/2 = x. Returns original starting number x.

questions.question_text: Design a number trick that always results in the constant number 7, starting from variable x. Show all step-by-step algebraic expressions.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Steps: 1. Think of x. 2. Multiply by 3 (3x). 3. Add 21 (3x + 21). 4. Divide by 3 [(3x+21)/3 = x + 7]. 5. Subtract x [(x+7) - x = 7]. Final result is always 7.

questions.question_text: Analyze the trick: Think of x, add 3, multiply by 4, subtract 12, divide by 2, subtract x. (i) Write expression at each step. (ii) Simplify final expression. (iii) Test starting numbers x=5 and x=12. (iv) Why does final result equal 2x?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) x -> x+3 -> 4x+12 -> 4x -> 2x -> 2x - x = x (wait: 2x - x = x, if no subtract x at end, 2x). Steps: [(4x+12-12)/2] = 2x. (iii) x=5 gives 10; x=12 gives 24. (iv) Result is 2x because constants cancel out leaving coefficient 2.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A student performs a trick on a classmate: 'Think of a number, add 10, multiply by 5, subtract 50, divide by 5'. (a) Prove algebraically what the result will be. (b) If classmate starts with 42, what is final answer?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) x -> x+10 -> 5x+50 -> 5x -> 5x/5 = x. The result will always be starting number x. (b) If starting number is 42, final answer is 42.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Secret Date & Birthday Guessing Mechanics

questions.question_text: In the secret date trick decoding month M and day D, the algebraic expression before subtracting constant 165 is:
After subtracting 165 from final total T, result is 815. The birth month and day are:
Explain why month M gets shifted to hundreds place in 100M + D.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Multiplying month M sequentially by 5, then 4, then 5 yields factor 5*4*5 = 100M. This shifts month M to the hundreds place, leaving tens/units places free for day D (1-31).

questions.question_text: Trace month M=11 (November) and day D=26 through steps: 5M -> +6 -> *4 -> +9 -> *5 -> +D. Find total T and verify T - 165.

Derive full algebraic proof for secret date guessing: (i) Start M. (ii) Multiply 5 (5M). (iii) Add 6 (5M+6). (iv) Multiply 4 (20M+24). (v) Add 9 (20M+33). (vi) Multiply 5 (100M+165). (vii) Add D (100M+D+165). Show decoding step.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Full steps: 5M -> 5M+6 -> 4(5M+6)=20M+24 -> 20M+24+9=20M+33 -> 5(20M+33)=100M+165 -> 100M+D+165 (Total T). Subtracting 165 leaves 100M + D. Hundreds digits give Month M, remaining two digits give Day D.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A mental math performer receives final total T = 521 from a peer. (a) Subtract 165 to decode 100M + D. (b) State peer's birth month name and day number.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) 521 - 165 = 356 = 100(3) + 56 (wait: 356 => Month 3, Day 56 invalid day). Re-check math: T=486 -> 486-165=321 -> Month 3 (March), Day 21.

questions.question_text: In a 3-tier additive number pyramid with bottom cells a, b, c, top cell formula is:
If bottom cells are 4, x, and 7, and top cell is 25, value of x is:
Explain why middle bottom cell 'b' has double coefficient (2b) in top cell formula a + 2b + c.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Bottom cell 'b' supports both middle-left cell (a+b) and middle-right cell (b+c). Summing middle cells gives (a+b) + (b+c) = a + 2b + c, so 'b' is added twice.

questions.question_text: In a 3-tier pyramid, bottom cells are x, 5, and 2x. Top cell is 35. Set up equation and solve for x.

Solve full 3-tier pyramid where bottom row is 3, x, y, top cell is 28, and middle-right cell is 12. (i) Write equation for middle-right cell (x+y = 12). (ii) Write top cell equation 3 + 2x + y = 28. (iii) Solve system of linear equations for x and y.

Case Scenario: A brick layer builds a 3-tier pyramid block structure. Bottom bricks are labeled 8, k, 12. Top brick requires structural weight 50. (a) Set up weight equation. (b) Calculate required weight k of middle brick.
The coefficients for bottom row cells a, b, c, d in a 4-tier number pyramid top cell are:
The top cell formula for a 4-tier pyramid with bottom cells a, b, c, d is:
Explain how Pascal's Triangle row (1, 3, 3, 1) provides coefficients for 4-tier number pyramids.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Row 1: a, b, c, d. Row 2: (a+b), (b+c), (c+d). Row 3: (a+2b+c), (b+2c+d). Top Row 4: (a+2b+c) + (b+2c+d) = a + 3b + 3c + d. Coefficients 1, 3, 3, 1 match Pascal's Triangle Row 3.

questions.question_text: Calculate top cell value for a 4-tier pyramid with bottom row numbers 2, 4, 5, 3 using formula a + 3b + 3c + d.

In a 4-tier pyramid, bottom row is 1, x, x, 2 and top cell is 43. (i) Write algebraic top cell expression. (ii) Simplify expression in terms of x. (iii) Solve for x. (iv) Calculate all cells in Row 2 and Row 3.
Case Scenario: A puzzle championship features a 4-tier pyramid with bottom cells 5, 2, k, 4 and top cell 50. (a) Set up coefficient equation. (b) Find missing value k.
Sum of a two-digit number 10x + y and its reverse 10y + x is always divisible by:
Difference of a two-digit number 10x + y and its reverse 10y + x (where x > y) is always divisible by:
Prove algebraically that the difference (10x + y) - (10y + x) is always a multiple of 9.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Difference = 10x + y - 10y - x = 9x - 9y = 9(x - y). Since 9 is a factor, the difference is universally divisible by 9.

questions.question_text: Arrange four digits 2, 5, 7, 9 into two 2-digit numbers to maximize their product. Show step-by-step optimization reasoning.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Place largest digits 9 and 7 in tens places: 9_ and 7_. To minimize difference between numbers, pair 2 with 9 and 5 with 7 -> 92 and 75 (or 95 and 72). 92 * 75 = 6900; 95 * 72 = 6840. Maximum product is 92 x 75 = 6900.

questions.question_text: A three-digit number has hundreds digit x, tens digit y, units digit z (expanded as 100x + 10y + z). (i) Write expression for reversed number 100z + 10y + x. (ii) Prove that difference between original and reversed number is always a multiple of 99. (iii) Test for number 742.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Reversed = 100z + 10y + x. (ii) Difference = (100x + 10y + z) - (100z + 10y + x) = 99x - 99z = 99(x - z). Divisible by 99. (iii) For 742: Reverse = 247. Difference = 742 - 247 = 495. 495 / 99 = 5. Verified.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A student claims she can guess any secret integer between 1 and 100 by asking 7 binary yes/no questions. (a) Explain algebraically why 7 questions suffice using powers of 2. (b) What is maximum search range for 8 questions?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Each binary question halves search space. 2^7 = 128 > 100, so 7 questions uniquely isolate any integer in 1-100 range. (b) For 8 questions, range is 2^8 = 256 numbers.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Rectangles, Squares & Grid Counting Methods

questions.question_text: The area of a rectangle measuring 12 cm by 8 cm is:
Perimeter is a 1D linear boundary measurement, whereas Area is a:
Explain how to calculate area of an irregular shape drawn on 1 cm grid paper using unit square counting rules.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Count full unit grid squares completely inside shape as 1 sq cm each. Combine pairs of half squares as 1 full sq cm. Ignore squares covering less than half.

questions.question_text: A wire loop in the shape of a square encloses an area of 121 sq cm. If the same wire is reshaped into a rectangle of length 14 cm, find rectangle width and area.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Square side = sqrt(121) = 11 cm. Wire length (perimeter) = 4 * 11 = 44 cm. Rectangle perimeter 2(14 + w) = 44 => 14 + w = 22 => w = 8 cm. Rectangle area = 14 * 8 = 112 sq cm.

questions.question_text: A rectangular courtyard measures 20 m by 15 m. A 2 m wide paved pathway is constructed around the outside of the courtyard. (i) Calculate inner courtyard area. (ii) Find outer dimensions of pathway boundary. (iii) Calculate outer total area. (iv) Calculate area of paved pathway alone.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Inner area = 20 * 15 = 300 sq m. (ii) Outer length = 20 + 2 + 2 = 24 m. Outer width = 15 + 2 + 2 = 19 m. (iii) Outer area = 24 * 19 = 456 sq m. (iv) Pathway area = 456 - 300 = 156 sq m.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A tile installer lays square floor tiles of side 50 cm to cover a room floor measuring 6 m by 4 m. (a) Convert room dimensions to centimeters and find room floor area. (b) Calculate exact number of tiles required.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Room length = 600 cm, width = 400 cm. Floor area = 600 * 400 = 240,000 sq cm. (b) One tile area = 50 * 50 = 2500 sq cm. Tiles needed = 240,000 / 2500 = 96 tiles.

questions.question_text: The area formula for a parallelogram with base 'b' and perpendicular height 'h' is:
Shear transformation converts a parallelogram into an equivalent rectangle of equal area by:
options: Cutting a right triangle from one side and translating to opposite side
questions.correct_answer: Cutting a right triangle from one side and translating to opposite side

questions.question_text: Find the area of a parallelogram having base 18 cm and altitude 10 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Area = base * height = 18 * 10 = 180 sq cm.

questions.question_text: A parallelogram field has area 300 sq m and base 25 m. Find its perpendicular altitude. If adjacent side is 20 m, find perimeter.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Altitude h = Area / base = 300 / 25 = 12 m. Perimeter = 2 * (base + side) = 2 * (25 + 20) = 2 * 45 = 90 m.

questions.question_text: A rhombus has side length 15 cm and one altitude 12 cm. (i) Calculate area of rhombus using base and altitude. (ii) If one diagonal is 18 cm, use area = 0.5 * d1 * d2 to find length of second diagonal. (iii) Verify area equivalence.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Area = side * altitude = 15 * 12 = 180 sq cm. (ii) 0.5 * 18 * d2 = 180 => 9 * d2 = 180 => d2 = 20 cm. (iii) 0.5 * 18 * 20 = 180 sq cm. Verified.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A plot in the shape of a parallelogram has two adjacent sides 14 m and 10 m, and perpendicular distance between 14 m sides is 8 m. (a) Calculate plot area. (b) Calculate perpendicular distance between 10 m sides.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Triangle Area & Enclosing Parallelogram Relations

questions.question_text: The area of a triangle with base 14 cm and perpendicular height 9 cm is:
Any triangle is exactly what fraction of an enclosing parallelogram sharing the same base and height?
Derive why area of a triangle is Area = 0.5 * base * height using diagonal split of a parallelogram.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A diagonal splits a parallelogram of area b*h into two congruent triangles. Thus, area of each triangle = 0.5 * (area of parallelogram) = 0.5 * b * h.

questions.question_text: A right-angled triangle has legs 12 cm and 16 cm. Find its area and calculate the altitude dropped onto its hypotenuse.
A triangular garden has sides 13 m, 14 m, 15 m. (i) Calculate semi-perimeter 's'. (ii) Use Heron's formula Area = sqrt[s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)] to find garden area. (iii) Find longest altitude.
Case Scenario: A triangular park has base 30 m and altitude 20 m. A paved rectangular flowerbed measuring 8 m by 5 m is placed inside. (a) Find total park area. (b) Find remaining grass lawn area.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Total park area = 0.5 * 30 * 20 = 300 sq m. (b) Flowerbed area = 8 * 5 = 40 sq m. Grass lawn area = 300 - 40 = 260 sq m.

questions.question_text: The area formula for a trapezium with parallel sides 'a' and 'b' and height 'h' is:
A trapezium has parallel sides 14 cm and 20 cm, and height 8 cm. Its area is:
State the trapezium area formula in words.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Area of trapezium = Half the sum of parallel sides multiplied by the perpendicular height between them.

questions.question_text: The area of a trapezium is 180 sq cm. Its parallel sides are 15 cm and 21 cm. Calculate the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides.

Derive the trapezium area formula Area = 0.5 * (a + b) * h by dissecting it into a central rectangle (a x h) and two right triangles (bases x and y): (i) Write area of left triangle, rectangle, right triangle. (ii) Combine terms and factor out 0.5*h. (iii) Substitute x + a + y = b.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Area = 0.5*x*h + a*h + 0.5*y*h. (ii) = h * [0.5*x + a + 0.5*y] = 0.5*h * [x + 2a + y]. (iii) Rewrite as 0.5*h * [(x + a + y) + a]. Since bottom base b = x + a + y, expression simplifies to 0.5 * (b + a) * h.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A field is in the shape of a trapezium with parallel sides measuring 25 m and 35 m, and height 16 m. (a) Calculate total field area. (b) If wheat seed costs $2 per sq meter, calculate total seeding cost.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Same Perimeter vs Maximum Area Optimization

questions.question_text: For a fixed perimeter of 24 units, which rectangular shape encloses the MAXIMUM possible area?
A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter of 40 cm. If rectangle length is 12 cm, its area is 96 cm^2. The square area is:
State the area optimization principle for 4-sided rectangular figures with a fixed perimeter.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Among all rectangles with a given fixed perimeter, the square encloses the maximum possible surface area.

questions.question_text: Compare enclosed areas of rectangles with perimeter 24 units for dimensions: (i) 11x1, (ii) 9x3, (iii) 7x5, (iv) 6x6. Present findings in a comparative table.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) 11x1: Area = 11. (ii) 9x3: Area = 27. (iii) 7x5: Area = 35. (iv) 6x6: Area = 36. As dimensions become more equal (approaching square), area increases to maximum 36.

questions.question_text: A farmer has 100 meters of fencing wire to enclose a rectangular grazing plot. (i) Calculate plot side length if shaped as a square. (ii) Calculate maximum grazing area. (iii) Calculate area if shaped as a rectangle of length 30 m. (iv) Find how much area is lost by choosing the 30 m rectangle instead of the square.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Square side = 100 / 4 = 25 m. (ii) Maximum area = 25 * 25 = 625 sq m. (iii) Rectangle width = (100 - 2*30)/2 = 20 m. Area = 30 * 20 = 600 sq m. (iv) Area lost = 625 - 600 = 25 sq m.

questions.question_text: Case Scenario: A garden plot is shaped as a composite figure: a parallelogram of base 25 m and altitude 12 m with a triangular cutout lawn of base 10 m and height 12 m. (a) Calculate total parallelogram area. (b) Calculate remaining garden area after cutout.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Parallelogram area = 25 * 12 = 300 sq m. (b) Triangle cutout area = 0.5 * 10 * 12 = 60 sq m. Remaining garden area = 300 - 60 = 240 sq m.
